title: HTML Entity Parser
statement:
The string `text` holds HTML source. Decode it: every occurrence of one of the six entities in the table becomes the single character it stands for, and the decoded string is returned.

| Entity | Character |
|---|---|
| `"` | `"` |
| `'` | `'` |
| `&` | `&` |
| `>` | `>` |
| `<` | `<` |
| `⁄` | `/` |

- An entity must match the table exactly, including case and the closing `;`. Anything else (such as `&ambassador;`, `>` or `&amp` with no semicolon) is copied unchanged.
- Decode in one left-to-right pass over `text`: a character produced by a replacement is never joined with the text after it to form a new entity, so `&lt;` decodes to `<`.
constraints: text may contain any of the 256 ASCII characters

examples.name: Example 1
input: & is an HTML entity but &ambassador; is not.
examples.expected: & is an HTML entity but &ambassador; is not.

input: no entities here; just text & more text

notes:
## Intuition

Every entity starts with `&`, ends with `;`, and is at most 7 characters long (`⁄`). So most characters are copied as they are; only at an `&` do we need to look a few characters ahead and ask a table whether that word is a known entity. Calling a global replace once per entity would be wrong: decoding `&` first and `<` afterwards turns `&lt;` into `<` instead of `<`.

## Approach

1. Put the six entities in a map `symbols` from entity text to its character.
2. Walk `text` with an index `i`, collecting output pieces in `result`.
3. At an `&`, take the next 7 characters as `chunk` and find the first `;` in it.
4. If there is one and `chunk` up to it (`entity`) is in the map, push its character and jump `i` past the whole entity.
5. Otherwise push `text[i]` unchanged and move one step. Join `result` at the end.

## Example 1, step by step

`text = "& is an HTML entity but &ambassador; is not."`. At `i = 0` the chunk is `"& i"`, its `;` is at 4, so `entity = "&"`, which the map knows: push `&` and jump to `i = 5`. Plain characters are copied one by one. At the second `&` the chunk is `"&ambass"` with no `;`, so the `&` is copied and the scan continues through `ambassador;` unchanged. The answer is `"& is an HTML entity but &ambassador; is not."`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each character is copied once, and each `&` looks at most 7 characters ahead.
- Space: O(n) for the output pieces.

## Pitfalls

- Never decode the output again: `&gt;` must become `>`, not `>`.
- Searching for the next `;` across the whole rest of the string is O(n) per `&`; bound the look-ahead to 7 characters.
- Matching is exact: `>` and `&amp` (no semicolon) are left alone.
- Building the answer with repeated `+=` in a loop is fine in JavaScript but slow in Java; use a builder.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `symbols` | map from each entity to the character it stands for |
| `result` | pieces of the decoded string, in order |
| `i` | index of the next unread character of `text` |
| `chunk` | up to 7 characters starting at an `&` |
| `semicolon` | position of the first `;` inside `chunk`, or -1 |
| `entity` | `chunk` up to and including that `;` |
